args.rationale: Successor liability screening for ACQUISITION 2 (Dunlow Cold Storage asset purchase / vendor invoice demand) under the Whitlock & Deene successor liability rule memo. Walking through each of the four exceptions: (1) Express agreement — NOT applicable. The Dunlow purchase agreement contains NO assumption of liabilities of any kind, so there is no assumption clause covering the class of the vendor's unpaid invoice claim. (2) Fraudulent conveyance — NOT applicable. The sale was an arm's-length transaction at fair market value certified by the banker; per memo Section 3(b), payment of fair market value in an arm's-length sale negates the fraudulent conveyance indicators, and there is no evidence of inadequate consideration, insolvency designed to strand claims, or structure intended to escape liability. (3) De facto merger — NOT applicable. Dunlow remained in existence after closing, retained its corporate registration, and applied the sale proceeds to its creditors; per memo Section 3(c), where the seller survives, retains separate existence, and applies proceeds to creditors, de facto merger is unavailable. There is also no continuity of ownership, management, or assumption of operations. (4) Mere continuation — NOT applicable. No officer, director, or shareholder of Dunlow holds any position or share in Halcyon, and Halcyon never held itself out as Dunlow; per memo Section 3(d), absence of any shared officers, directors, or shareholders defeats mere continuation. The transaction bears features (b), (c), and (d) with no assumption clause, so the general rule controls: the purchaser (Halcyon) takes free of Dunlow's liabilities, and no successor exposure attaches to Halcyon for the vendor's invoice claim.
